Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

3. Material 



3.1 Carbon Stee/ 

3.1 .1 When blade and handle forged together the steel shall have the following composition : 

Percent 
Carbon 1-20-1 -30 

Manganese 0-20-0-45 

Silicon 0-10-0-35 

Sulphur 025, Max 

Phosphorus 0035, Max 

Chromium 0-1 0-0-40

the composition of steel used shall be as follows :

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The knife shall be so forged as to be symmetrical about its central plane. The cutting edge on the blade 
shall be on the central plane. The handle shall provide a good grip and the knife shall have a balanced feel 
when handled by the surgeon. 

4.2 The cutting edge on the blade portion shall be formed by hollow grinding. 

4.3 The knife shall be highly polished and free from any blemishes. All edges other than the cutting edge, 
shall be rounded and nowhere sharp. All surfaces shall be finished smooth and free from burrs, pits, tool 
marks and other surface defects. The edges of the handle shall be chamfered. Handle surface shall have 
longitudinal grooves for good grip. 

4.4 No cutting edge shall have a nick greater than 0-10 mm on it. No cutting edge shall contain more 
than two nicks of size greater than 005 mm on it. Such nicks, if present, shall be not closer than 4 mm 
apart. There shall be no feathers, gags or other defects on the cutting edge. 

4.5 Knives made from stainless steel shall be passivated. When made from carbon steel, the knife shall be 
plated chromium over nickel, except the cutting edge which shall not be plated. The plating shall conform 
to Service Grade No. 2 of IS : 1068-1968 ' Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on 
iron and steel {first revision)'. 

4.6 The tip of the knife hook shall be rounded. 

5. Heat Treatment — The working end shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 600-700 HV. 
The hardness of handle shall be not less than 140 l-IV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Corrosion Resistance Test ( for Stainless Steel Only ) — Scrub the knife with soap and warm water, rinse 
in hot water and then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the knife, immerse in copper sulphate solution at 
room temperature for six minutes and wash with fresh water or wet cotton wool. 

The copper sulphate solution shall be made up as follows: 

Copper sulphate (CuSO^-SH-.O) 40 g 

Sulphuric acid (H.SOJ (sp gr 1 -84) 100 g 

Distilled water [see IS : 1070-1960 Specification 900 ml 

for water, distilled quality (revised)] 

There shall be no :'ed stains or spots on the knife after the test but dulling of the polished surface may be 
permitted. 

6.2 The cutting edge shall be examined under a magnification of 10 x . The edge shall satisfy the require- 
ments given in 4.4. 

7. Marking —The knife shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words 'SS' shall be marked on knives made of stainless steel. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution . 

8. Packing —The blade portion of carbon steel knives shall be coated with a corrosion resisting substance. 
The knives shall be individually wrapped in moisture-proof paper or put in polyethylene bags and then packed 
in cardboard cartons.
